title: Assistant Teaching Professor - Finance
description:
Position Overview

This position is a full-time, academic-year, non-tenure-track
Assistant Teaching Professor position in the School of Business at
the University of Kansas. The position's primary responsibility is
teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Finance and
Economics, with a particular emphasis on courses supporting the
Bicknell Certificate in Personal Finance, KU's CFP program within
the School of Business: 
https://business.ku.edu/undergraduate-programs/degree-programs/bicknell-certificate-personal-finance
).

KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences,
perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and
colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest
in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where
people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each
other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is
seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging,
we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and
achieve remarkable things.

This position is subject to a 
collective bargaining agreement between The University of
Kansas and United Academics. UAKU is the exclusive representative
for the bargaining unit, and it is the candidate’s right to be a
member or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or
professional repercussions.

The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by
the effective date of the appointment. Any employment with the
University of Kansas is contingent upon satisfactory completion of
a background check.

Job Description

80% Teaching
Teach undergraduate or graduate level courses on various topics in
personal and household finance, personal financial planning,
insurance, economics, finance and/or foundations of business.
Potential course assignments for this position include FIN 330
Introduction to Financial Planning and Retirement and FIN 430
Financial Planning Capstone within the Bicknell Certificate in
Personal Finance, although other course assignments are expected as
the program expands. Duties include, but are not limited to,
instruction in the area of finance, course preparation,
consultatio n, and assignment of course grades. Courses may be
taught in online or on-campus formats, including at the Lawrence
and/or Leavenworth campuses. The typical course load for this
appointment is eight courses per academic year. Course load and
teaching assignments will be determined by the F inance Area
Director to best meet the needs of the School of Business. All
faculty members are expected to abide by area, school, and
university policies and procedures.

20% Service
Engage in service both within and outside the school and
university, including professional and scholarly engagement
activities that support instruction and student development.
Participate as an active member of the area and engage in
instruction-related activities beyond direct instruction. All
faculty members are expected to fulfill their share of service
duties needed to facilitate the efficient operation of the school.
May perform additional position-related activities as assigned by
the Dean or Area Director.

Required Qualifications


Possess a PhD in Finance or closely related discipline, OR an
MBA or other professional degree in a closely related discipline
plus a demonstrated record of scholarship and achievement, by the
start of the appointment.
Documented ability or high potential to successfully teach
across student populations, as demonstrated by prior experience in
teaching, training, leadership, or other relevant experience.

Additional Candidate Instruction

To be considered, candidates must submit an online application. A
complete application will include a:

Letter of application describing interest in KU, experience and
distinctive accomplishments,
Record of productivity in research and teaching as described in
CV,
Teaching statement and supplemental materials (e.g., teaching
portfolio, sample syllabi, teaching evaluations).

Letters of recommendation will be requested from selected
applicants as the search process moves beyond the initial screening
round.

Only complete application packages submitted online will be
considered.
